Write a suite to YAML

Source: R/suite.R
write_agent_suite.Rd

Serialises an `r4agent_suite` back to the YAML that [read_agent_suite()] reads, so a suite assembled in R can be committed next to the code it tests and read back unchanged. A suite that uses only built-in or registered graders by name round trips exactly.

Usage

write_agent_suite(suite, path = NULL)

Arguments

suite

An `r4agent_suite`.

path

Path to write to, or NULL to return the YAML as a string.

Value

The YAML text. Returned invisibly when written to `path`.

Details

A grader supplied as a function cannot be written: the file names a grader, it cannot carry the function's code. Such a case is still written, with every other field kept (`why`, `severity`, `slice`, `expect` and the rest), and a warning names it; on the way back in its grader falls to the default.

See also

[read_agent_suite()]

Examples

suite <- agent_suite(list(
  agent_case("billing-01", "When is my next invoice due?", "first",
             slice = "billing", grader = "contains",
             why = "Monthly plans bill on the first of the month."),
  agent_case("abstain-01", "Does the plan support SAML on the old portal?",
             family = "grounding", slice = "not answerable",
             severity = "high", grader = "abstain",
             why = "The docs do not say, so the only right answer is to say so.")
))
cat(write_agent_suite(suite))
#> cases:
#> - id: billing-01
#>   input: When is my next invoice due?
#>   expect: first
#>   family: task
#>   slice: billing
#>   severity: medium
#>   grader: contains
#>   why: Monthly plans bill on the first of the month.
#> - id: abstain-01
#>   input: Does the plan support SAML on the old portal?
#>   family: grounding
#>   slice: not answerable
#>   severity: high
#>   grader: abstain
#>   why: The docs do not say, so the only right answer is to say so.

# Round-trips through a file
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".yaml")
write_agent_suite(suite, f)
identical(length(read_agent_suite(f)), length(suite))
#> [1] TRUE
unlink(f)
